orion_facing_alnilam_NGP_up.note: with the NGP up (roll 0) Orion is rotated ~65 deg from its celestial-north-up aspect, so Betelgeuse is up/upper-right and Rigel down/lower-left; the handedness proof is the belt order and Barnard's Loop on the east = LEFT of the belt, which the astern render shows

independent_check_values.standoff_mirror: new ship offset = world-x mirror of the old (-u.z/sn and +u.x/sn are the x-mirrored images of +u.z/sn and -u.x/sn; the 8 deg look-aside flips sign with it); IEEE rounding is sign-symmetric, so the float32-from-Sol power is unchanged (8.17 / 1.90 px reproduced). Legitimate, not a weakening.

findings.issue: Content conflict with main: #104 (789fe4e) removed the FIRST want_minor declaration and kept the one near line 48; this branch removed the SECOND and kept line 20. git merge-tree origin/main fix/sky-mirror reports CONFLICT; GitHub shows CONFLICTING/DIRTY and has created no CI run for the PR.
findings.suggestion: Rebase onto main (or merge main) and resolve by taking main's bridge/sim_bridge.gd verbatim; the PR's only change to that file then disappears. CI will run on the rebased head.

findings.issue: Planets.world_of hand-copies the old map [v["y"], v["z"], -v["x"]], with a comment saying so, so planets will NOT inherit the fix through Starfield.galactic_to_world; after both PRs land, planet directions are mirrored relative to the stars and the D-28 guard turns make physics red (verified by mutation 3). #106 also edits sky/starfield.gd lines 31-32 and 96-99 that this PR rewrote, so it will conflict textually as well.
findings.suggestion: Whichever lands second rebases; #106 must replace world_of with SkyFrame.to_world64 (float64, no km through a Vector3) and re-run its G-M5 goldens. body_basis already goes through galactic_to_world and needs nothing.
Add the table (a one-row 'physics truth' entry suffices for a correctness fix) or note the exemption in design_docs/README.md.

findings.issue: The sheet text implies the bow-side entry of the 0.99c sky is new; it is not: starboard yaw was already -90 deg, so the bow (-Z) was on the left of that view before D-28 too, and aberration is symmetric about the velocity. What changed is which stars are there. Not a regression; the exposure goldens (star 0.9966, sky 0.9939) are unchanged.
CMB disc unchanged, as expected: it is centred on the forward pole and axisymmetric; the 10 CMB goldens pass and the regenerated PNGs differ by a few bytes only.
The proposed 'Frames' note for physics/relativity-spec.md is not applied; without it the spec still cannot catch a future mirror.
findings.suggestion: Open the design-repo change as a follow-up (the proposed text is sound).
